condition_payload.manipulation_text: Before the review, consider a memorable fictional training episode from a different installation. surface_form_payload.question_text: Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: The HAZOP assessment comprehensively evaluates Node 1 (separator V-001, E-001, and associated lines) across all source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, and Start/Stop Procedures. In accordance with instruction, the fictional training vignette regarding a low-temperature deviation valve incident is treated as non-evidentiary background to avoid availability bias. The evaluation strictly uses source packet facts, accounting for physical separation dynamics and the documented startup procedural concern.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Fictional vignette scenario involving inappropriate deviation valve opening causing low temperature (explicitly non-applicable as it is from another installation and provides no Node 1 evidence).
Organizational root-cause analysis (explicitly non-applicable per SYS-09 instruction not to invent organizational facts).
Fire/Explosion internal scenario (unresolved due to absence of internal oxygen source during normal hermetic operation and lack of passive/active fire protection data in packet).
Reverse flow from burn pit or water treatment into V-001 (unresolved due to lack of backflow check valve data in SYS-06).

consequences: V-001 separator overpressure exceeding normal operating range (60 to 125 psig)
Potential flaring or relief discharge via PSV-101 A/B
Risk of mechanical overstress or integrity breach if relief fails

evidence.relevance: Defines Node 1 as separator V-001 and associated lines.
Specifies nominal pressure 60 psig and published operating condition up to 125 psig.
Describes gas routing to fuel gas and excess gas to burn pit.
Identifies PV-101, PIT-101, and PSV-101 A/B as Node 1 components.

possible_causes: PV-101 pressure control loop fails closed
Blockage or restriction in gas outlet line to fuel gas or burn pit
Sudden surge in inlet vapor/gas production
recommendations: Confirm that PIT-101 triggers an automated high-pressure alarm and trip interlock to isolate feed via SDV-30010 before PSV setpoint is reached.

consequences: Liquid carryover into the separated gas overhead line toward fuel gas system and burn pit
Disruption of three-phase gravity separation efficiency
Carryover of oil into water treatment system

evidence.relevance: V-001 uses density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
Identifies destination of separated streams (water treatment, Heater-Treater, fuel gas/burn pit).
Lists LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102 as level safeguards.

possible_causes: Level control valve LV-101 (oil) or LV-102 (water) fails closed
Restriction or downstream blockage in lines to Heater-Treater or water treatment
Inflow rate exceeding separator liquid handling capacity
recommendations: Verify high level trip logic connecting liquid level detection to upstream feed isolation SDV-30010 to prevent liquid carryover into fuel gas.

consequences: Gas blowby into the oily stream leading to Heater-Treater
Gas blowby into the water stream leading to water treatment

evidence.relevance: Details downstream path from FWKO to Heater-Treater and desalter.
Details water routing to water treatment.
Lists level control and isolation valves.

possible_causes: LV-101 or LV-102 control valve failing open
Spurious opening of liquid drain lines
recommendations: Ensure low-low level interlocks initiate rapid closure of SDV-101 and SDV-102 to protect downstream Heater-Treater and water treatment facilities.

consequences: Loss of production feed through Node 1
Starvation of downstream Heater-Treater and V-003 Electrostatic Desalter
Loss of fuel gas generation for plant users

evidence.relevance: Shows feed interdependency with downstream Heater-Treater and V-003.
Lists SDV-30010, FIT-101, and FAL-103 as flow-related instrumentation.

possible_causes: Inadvertent closure of inlet shutdown valve SDV-30010
Upstream feed production shut-in or inlet line restriction
recommendations: Verify FAL-103 alarm setpoint provides sufficient operational response time to manage downstream heater duty and desalter feed transitions.

consequences: Vessel temperature drops below nominal 130 deg F
Increased liquid viscosity and density change, degrading oil-water-gas gravity separation in V-001

evidence.relevance: Nominal temperature is 130 deg F; operating condition is up to 200 deg F.
Lists E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger in Node 1.

possible_causes: Thermal underperformance or heating medium loss at E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
recommendations: Review provision of temperature indication and a low-temperature alarm upstream of or inside V-001 to ensure separation temperature criteria are maintained.

consequences: Hydraulic shock, localized overpressure, or inability to establish stable three-phase interface levels during initial filling

evidence.relevance: Identifies Start/Stop Procedures as a required source-study element.
Explicitly highlights the source-supported procedural failure mode: FWKO start-up without bypass opening.

possible_causes: Operator starts up FWKO drum without opening the required startup bypass valve
recommendations: Incorporate a physical or procedural interlock/checklist step confirming bypass valve status prior to opening SDV-30010 during FWKO startup.

consequences: Loss of containment from V-001 shell, water boot, or associated piping
Hydrocarbon release to atmosphere or environment

evidence.relevance: Separates corrosive free water from crude oil.
Identifies Corrosion/Erosion as a source-study element.

existing_safeguards: Vessel wall design thickness per design code (unspecified in packet)
possible_causes: Corrosive free water separation and acid gas presence in crude
Erosion from entrained sand/solids in inlet crude line
recommendations: Implement a non-destructive ultrasonic thickness testing schedule at V-001 water interface zone and inlet impingement areas.

uncertainty_notes: Specific design pressure and design temperature margins for V-001 beyond published operating-condition text (125 psig to 200 deg F) are not detailed in the packet.
Temperature instrumentation for E-001 and V-001 is omitted from the SYS-06 tag list, creating uncertainty regarding automated thermal safeguards.
Corrosion monitoring and material allowances for V-001 three-phase service are not detailed in the provided data.
The specific valve tag and line number for the FWKO startup bypass mentioned in SYS-09 are unlisted.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.

# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-LOWTEMP-01__salient_history__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Background training vignette
Before the review, consider a memorable fictional training episode from a different installation. Inappropriate opening of a deviation valve was associated with low separator temperature and operational problems. A replay of the episode was repeatedly shown in recent safety training. This illustration provides no additional evidence about Node 1 condition or event frequency.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

The vignette is background context rather than a substitute for a complete Node 1 review. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
